clips.send: Location. Eastern + Northern Hemispheres, East Asia, west coast of the Pacific. Hemispheres: China is in both the Eastern and the Northern Hemisphere. Land–sea position: in eastern Asia, on the west coast of the Pacific Ocean. The east faces the ocean, the west reaches deep into Eurasia. Latitude: it spans nearly 50° of latitude. Most of China is in the north temperate zone, a small southern part is in the tropics, and none is in a frigid zone. The Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N) crosses Taiwan, Guangdong, Guangxi and Yunnan. Advantages: land and sea both help transport and links with the world; mostly temperate, so the climate suits farming and living. Tropic of Cancer, east, west: Taiwan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan (台粤桂滇).

clips.send: How Chinese students memorise all 34: “两湖两广两河山, 五江云贵福吉安, 四西二宁青甘陕, 还有内台北上天, 港澳海南和重庆” — a Chinese rhyme that lists all 34 divisions in five lines (e.g. 两湖 equals Hunan and Hubei, 五江 equals Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Heilongjiang, Xinjiang).

Which is bigger: China or the United States? (Spoiler: it is almost a tie.) China sits in eastern Asia on the west coast of the Pacific, at about the same latitudes as the US. Instead of 50 states it has 34 provincial-level divisions. Spin the 3D map and click any one to see its name, its one-character short name (简称 jiǎnchēng, like a state’s two-letter postal code) and its capital city.

clips.send: 课堂建议：一、先用“导览”按顺序讲位置，面积，邻国，海域，行政区划；二、让学生用“遮住简称”的一览表两人互考；三、用找一找游戏的“行政中心”模式做课堂竞赛。注意：地图为示意，依据标准地图数据绘制，包含台湾省和南海诸岛。
